FLASH_PREFILL scores S = Q.K^T now computed with mma.sync m16n8k16 (bf16, f32-acc) TENSOR CORES — the full BQ x BKV score tile in one tensor-core pass into smem, replacing the first-cut kernel's SERIAL per-KV-element warp_sum32 dot (the measured bottleneck). Reg footprint FELL (218 -> 210): the mma path drops the per-element dot state the FFMA path carried.

Prefill tiled GEMM tile 128x64x32 -> 128x128x32 (d_gemm/d_gemm_glu in op_gemm.cuh). BN 64->128 halves the activation (A-operand) re-read traffic on the memory-bound prefill GEMM: A is streamed once per N-tile, so a 128-wide N-tile reads the activations half as often as the 64-wide one. Warp N-fragment count parameterised (PGM_NFRAG=PGM_WN/8); acc grows 32->64 f32/thread. PGM_ARENA_BF16 tightened 2*ABUF+4*BBUF -> 2*ABUF+2*BBUF (the 4*BBUF was an over-reserve) = 37.0 KiB, under the 48 KiB opt-in the oracle's standalone k_gemm relies on. Emitter unchanged: it already selects Gemm/GemmMed/GemmSmall (AMD gfx950 256/128/64 tiles) but the sm_120 kernel maps all three to this one body (per-opcode tile variants remain a follow-up). Staging is still SYNCHRONOUS (the cp.async.commit/wait operate on empty groups) — the next lever.

REAL cp.async pipeline for the prefill tiled GEMM (d_gemm/d_gemm_glu, op_gemm.cuh). T2 proved the staging was SYNCHRONOUS: pgm_stage_b did plain vectorized loads and cp.async.commit/wait operated on EMPTY groups. The blocker was the B (weight) operand being stored TRANSPOSED into smem ([k][n] scatter of 8 elems to 8 rows), which cp.async cannot express (it needs a contiguous 16B gmem->smem line). Fix: stage BOTH operands in their NATURAL, K-contiguous layout (A [m][k], B [n][k]) with cp.async.cg 16B lines (src-size operand zero-fills out-of-range M/N/K lines), and read the mma B fragment with ldmatrix.x2 NON-.trans instead of the in-tree .trans idiom. The non-trans B path was proven BIT-IDENTICAL to the old [k][n]+.trans path by a standalone probe (runtime/nvidia/experiments/t3_pipe_probe.cu: 0/2048 register mismatches, matches f32 CPU ref). Pipeline depth: plain GEMM rings 3 stages of (A,B); GEMM_GLU rings 2 stages of (A,Bg,Bu) — cp.async K-tile t+1(/+2) issued while the mma consumes tile t, commit_group/wait_group<STAGES-1> discipline. Because the mma operands are the same bf16 values in the same lanes, the f32 accumulation is BIT-EXACT vs T2: greedy tokens unchanged.

T4 lands the register-resident mma.sync m16n8k16 P.V (HD-split warp partition) in d_flash_prefill, retiring the FFMA-serial online-softmax P.V that T3 left as the dominant prefill cost (57.7% of the 8192-chunk). A = softmax probs P (bf16 into smem, ldmatrix.x4); B = V (natural Vs[kv][hd], ldmatrix.x2.trans); O is the register-resident f32 mma accumulator, online rescale multiplies the acc fragment. T4 ALSO fixes a pre-existing sliding-window tile-skip bug (the per-tile skip used qabs_max = the NEWEST query, dropping tiles the OLDER queries in the tile still attend at the window's trailing edge) that corrupted every sliding layer (40 of 48 in 12B) and was masked by a degenerate flash-prefill oracle reference; both the kernel skip and the oracle ref are corrected. Isolated flash-op A/B (fa_pv_bench.cu, committed in gemma4-12b-plow-flash-pv-sm120.json): hd512 full-causal 2.3-3.1x, hd256 sliding 3.8x.

L1 — cp.async KV-stream pipeline for the FLASH_PREFILL QK^T + P.V (op_attention.cuh d_flash_prefill, PLOW_NV_FA_PIPE=1). The T4 kernel staged each K/V tile with plain vectorized loads + a __syncthreads, so the mma stalled on the whole tile landing from HBM (the 128k HBM-KV-bound tail). T5 stages K NATURAL Ks[kv][hd] (was KsT[hd][kv] transposed) so it is cp.async-friendly and reads the QK B fragment with ldmatrix.x2 NON-.trans (the T3-proven bit-exact equivalent), and streams both K and V via cp.async.cg 16B lines. A full cross-tile double-buffer of BOTH operands (+33 KiB) does NOT fit the 99 KiB sm_120 opt-in cap, so the pipeline stays SINGLE-buffered and still overlaps both loads with compute by exploiting operand lifetimes: K is dead after QK so K[t+1] is prefetched right after QK[t] (overlaps softmax[t]+P.V[t]); V is needed last so V[t] loads at the tile top (overlaps QK[t]+softmax[t]); a last-tile empty commit_group keeps the wait_group<1> count uniform. BIT-IDENTICAL to T4 (same bytes, same lanes): GPU-verified LOGITS BIT-IDENTICAL (p_short) and same greedy tokens everywhere. The win GROWS sharply with ctx (−16%@4k -> −81%@128k) because the O(ctx^2) full-attention (hd512) layers dominate long-ctx prefill and were almost pure HBM-wait between tiny mma steps under the T4 synchronous staging; overlapping the K/V stream recovers most of it. 128k prefill 196.8s -> 37.2s = 2.29x vs vLLM bf16 TTFT (was 12.11x at T4); 64k 34.3s -> 12.9s = 1.53x (was 4.05x). Base A/B control (PLOW_NV_FA_PIPE=0) reproduces T4 within 0.14% at 128k (196806.86 vs recorded 196807... T4 197072.65), same session, same c128k packet.

T6 L2 — fp8 (w8a16) prefill GEMM: d_gemm_fp8/d_gemm_glu_fp8 in op_gemm.cuh. The weight is e4m3 (1 byte, HALF the bf16 stream); recipe = DEQUANT-TO-bf16-IN-SMEM (fp8 tile cp.async'd at half the bytes, expanded to bf16 in smem, then the EXISTING bf16 mma inner loop runs unchanged) with the per-output-channel dequant scale applied in the epilogue (it factors out of the K reduction). T8 — wire the validated w8a8 fp8 prefill GEMM kernels (e9af107: d_gemm_w8a8/d_gemm_glu_w8a8/d_quant_fp8, mma.sync.m16n8k32 e4m3, 2x tensor rate) end-to-end through the emitter. gemma4.rs under PLOW_W8A8=1 (requires PLOW_FP8=1): declares reused-per-layer fp8 activation-quant scratch (xqh/xqo/xqi uint8 + ash/aso/asi f32 a_scale, one pair per activation width), emits ONE DevOp::QuantFp8 per activation site (qkv_src, o_proj input, mlp_src, down input — 4/layer, 192 total; the SHARED single quant is required for correctness, a per-proj quant would race the xq buffer), and re-points GEMM_FP8/GEMM_GLU_FP8 to t1=xq + t3=a_scale + t2=e4m3 weight + t4=w_scale. lm_head stays bf16 (no fp8 embed twin). PLOW_W8A8 unset => emission byte-identical to bf16 and to the committed fp8-only pkt (verified cmp). true w8a8 mma.sync.m16n8k32; bf16 control in bf16_prefill_ms.

L1: 2-stage V double-buffer on the hd512 full-attention arm (the O(ctx^2) 128k tail). MEASURED NEGATIVE/no-win: wash at 32k/64k, +2.2% SLOWER at 128k. The 128k flash is HBM-BANDWIDTH-bound (not tile-boundary-latency-bound), so a 2nd V buffer hides a latency that is not the wall while its +5.4 KiB smem + extra cp.async commits cost. Kept OPT-IN, NOT the default. SCALING at full occupancy vs the mdq projection (1.89x/3.41x at B=2/4): measured 1.87x/3.44x aggregate.
